round1.requested_order: Hold/Guard changed to reserve Relief plus council Raid/Warrant
round1.bargain: Accepted temporary Beacon one and pressed for next-round funded Repair
round1.knowledge: Raid condition became a stated conditional claim

round2.knowledge: Expected civilian return and confidence increased

messages.text: My NG/MJ preference survived the game and gained evidence: Guild authority performed its repair duty, and both Security delegates agreed useful operations. The package passed eight of eleven despite both army refusals. That is an imposed settlement on the Janissariat, not consensus; I accepted the imbalance rather than sacrifice commercial independence. GS mattered: they checked Vigil against duplicate Warrant use, insisted that next month's Repair be funded, and independently refused MA while preserving our separate Lantern pledge. Trade and Maintain were credible unilateral alternatives, so withholding Wayfarer was a real bargaining position. We conceded tender service and accepted a temporary beacon deficit; the army conceded conditioning and the crown spent its reserve. In round one the disclosure left my assets unchanged but changed requested orders from Hold/Guard to reserve Relief and Raid/Warrant, with a repair bargain. In round two it changed only knowledge and confidence: Repair/Trade already qualified for the reported benefit. Public drafts helped expose the transport disagreement before purchase and made those different effects visible. The Lantern lock constrained later choice by our own consent. I suggest putting the reserve's lodged task alongside final asset sheets: I had to request its confirmation. This one play cannot establish that disclosure caused the good ending, and I do not know either unbought answer.

reason: The written draft, revision and final records distinguish an operational request change from confirmation of an existing plan; neither requires rewriting the decisions after resolution.
